thread:
Aisha (support): FYI: customer ClearLedger opened a support ticket asking for deterministic JSON streaming for chat + fncall. They need parseable objects per frame so their ingestion can act on partial results.
Luca (product): Paste the ask pls — what's the absolute minimal contract they'd accept?
Aisha (support): TL;DR: 1) each stream chunk is a standalone valid JSON object (they prefer NDJSON), 2) fncall events must be emitted as a distinct object (tool/name/args/call_id), 3) must fallback to current streaming format if client opts out. Latency is a hard constraint.
Serena (sales): They said they'll convert to Dedicated if we can ship a supported beta. This could be a clear enterprise upsell. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ravi (eng-ml): Tech note — guaranteeing valid JSON per chunk means either buffering until object close (adds latency) or enforcing framed object emission at model/runtime level. Both have pros/cons.
Maya (eng-runtime): Two feasible approaches: (A) runtime framing shim (NDJSON or length-prefixed) that wraps token stream; low infra impact but slight added latency and edge cases with newlines inside fields. (B) model-emitted frames (structured tokens) — cleaner for clients but requires model/tokenizer changes and evaluation.
Luca (product): We need acceptance criteria and a rough schedule. Proposed acceptance: hosted + dedicated beta behind flag; NDJSON and len-pref framing supported; fncall objects standardized; SDK helpers + docs; p99 latency regression <= 50ms. Agree?
Ravi (eng-ml): Estimates: runtime shim prototype = ~5 dev-days (including tests), perf runs = 1-2 days. Model-level change = multi-week (4-6w) with eval loop.
Maya (eng-runtime): Runtime shim design: prefer length-prefix header to avoid newline ambiguity, but customer prefers NDJSON. We can support both: NDJSON as default beta and opt-in length-pref for strict clients. Need canary rollout + parse-fallback behavior when malformed JSON detected.
Aisha (support): ClearLedger insisted NDJSON is simplest for them. If we do length-pref, include example client code. I'll keep them in the loop.
Luca (product): Risk log: parse errors on partially emitted objects, increased token-to-response latency for short-turn chats, SDK churn. Mitigations: auto-fallback to token stream, telemetry to track parse-error-rate, and quick feature flag rollback.
Serena (sales): Customer needs ETA to decide payment. Can we promise a beta start date?
Maya (eng-runtime): Realistically: prototype + internal QA: 10 business days. Canary/beta with limited customers: additional 5 business days. So ~3 calendar weeks to beta if prioritized.
Luca (product): Decision: scope minimal runtime shim for initial beta. Ship NDJSON first, add len-pref later. Owners: Ravi + Maya implement, Luca owns spec + rollout, Aisha handles customer comms. I'll open a spec PR with acceptance criteria and sample SDK snippets.
ops-bot: Action created: product/feat/stream-framing. Assign to @Ravi and @Maya. Add canary ring and telemetry metrics: parse_error_rate, fallback_count, latency_delta_percent.
Ravi (eng-ml): Tests to add: nested JSON in assistant outputs, mid-object stream interruption, fncall object emission, and malformed-frame recovery.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also need to add a runtime flag to force fallback to legacy streaming per-request header.
Aisha (support): Updating the ticket and telling ClearLedger: tentative beta ~3 weeks; will share SDK examples and fallback details.
Luca (product): Follow-ups: (1) add client library helpers for NDJSON parsing, (2) internal perf dashboard comparing baseline vs framing by model/seq length, (3) schedule a decision review for model-level structured streaming after beta.
Serena (sales): I'll communicate conditional commitment to the customer. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
